summary: Ustaz Azlan continues the Prophet's SAW biography after the first revelation: the pause in revelation (about 40 days on the strongest view), the Prophet's SAW sadness and longing, the hadith of Jabir in which the Prophet SAW hears a call from the sky and sees Jibril in his true form filling the horizon, and then the revelation of Surah Al-Muddaththir. The ustaz explains five steps of mental and spiritual preparation from its opening verses, mentions other early surahs such as Al-Muzzammil, Al-Qalam and Ad-Duha, and conveys how hard it was for the Prophet SAW to begin a call against an entrenched system.
keyPoints: The pause in revelation is said to be anything from a few days to three years, but the ustaz prefers about 40 days or less.
The report of the Prophet SAW trying to throw himself off a mountain is not his own words and is criticised by scholars; it expresses deep grief.
In Jabir's hadith the Prophet SAW saw Jibril seated on a throne filling the space between heaven and earth, collapsed, and went home asking to be covered.
Surah Al-Muddaththir gives five steps: glorify Allah, purify your clothes, avoid wickedness, do not give expecting more, and be patient.
Surahs Al-Muzzammil, Al-Qalam and Ad-Duha are among the earliest and prepared the Prophet SAW mentally and spiritually.
The call must begin even when changing an entrenched system seems impossible, and its end must lead people to glorify Allah.

chapters.title: Step two: purify clothes and self
chapters.summary: Literal and spiritual meanings; calling to good begins with cleansing oneself.

chapters.title: Steps three to five
chapters.summary: Avoid wickedness, do not recount favours or expect return, and be patient with opposition.

lessons.title: Show gratitude by not wasting
lessons.body: Be thankful by not wasting food and by praying for the hungry.

lessons.title: Grief is not despair
lessons.body: The phrase about throwing himself down in Arab culture expresses sorrow and hope, not an act.

lessons.title: Allah calls gently
lessons.body: 'O you wrapped up' is affectionate, like the Prophet SAW calling Ali 'Aba Turab'.

lessons.title: Start good work by glorifying Allah
lessons.body: No problem is bigger than Allah's protection and no goal bigger than Him.

lessons.title: Cleanse yourself before you call
lessons.body: Before correcting others, look at yourself and your way of life.

lessons.title: Do not turn da'wah into a personality cult
lessons.body: If an approach makes people glorify a figure rather than Allah, that is a red flag.

lessons.title: Avoid bad words when criticised
lessons.body: The first instruction to the Prophet SAW: do not answer with foul words.

lessons.title: Give without expecting return
lessons.body: Do not feel you are doing a favour; it is Allah who chose you to spread good.

lessons.title: The path of da'wah will be hard and in waves
lessons.body: Be patient with opposition because there will be times you want to quit.

lessons.title: Repetition strengthens preparation
lessons.body: The Prophet SAW repeated Al-Alaq, Al-Muddaththir, Al-Muzzammil and Ad-Duha to firm up his spirit.

lessons.title: Begin even when it seems impossible
lessons.body: The Prophet SAW began with his closest family though the idol system was entrenched.

glossary.meaning: The period when revelation paused after the first revelation.
The one wrapped up; a gentle address to the Prophet SAW.
Foul words and deeds, including idol worship.
One of Allah's names, the One who gives without ceasing; related to reproaching (mann).
Reminding people of one's favours, which cancels the reward of charity.
Reciting the Quran slowly and clearly.

dalil.context: The Prophet SAW himself narrated; he was alarmed and went home asking to be covered.
dalil.translation: Then revelation paused for a while. While I was walking I heard a voice from the sky; I looked up and saw the angel who had come to me at Hira seated on a throne between heaven and earth.

dalil.context: Allah calls the Prophet SAW gently: O you wrapped up. (reference identified, verse number not stated)
Arise and warn. (reference identified, verse number not stated)
Glorify your Lord, the first step. (reference identified, verse number not stated)
dalil.translation: Proclaim the greatness of your Lord;

dalil.context: Purify your clothes, literally and spiritually. (reference identified, verse number not stated)
Avoid wickedness and bad words. (reference identified, verse number not stated)
Do not give expecting to receive more. (reference identified, verse number not stated)
dalil.translation: do not be overwhelmed and weaken;

dalil.context: Be patient for your Lord in facing opposition. (reference identified, verse number not stated)
dalil.translation: be steadfast in your Lord’s cause.

dalil.context: Do not cancel the reward of charity by reminders and hurt. (reference identified, verse number not stated)
dalil.translation: You who believe, do not cancel out your charitable deeds with reminders and hurtful words, like someone who spends his wealth only to be seen by people, not believing in God and the Last Day. Such a person is like a rock with earth on it: heavy rain falls and leaves it completely bare. Such people get no rewards for their works: God does not guide the disbelievers.

dalil.context: A rebuke to those who command good while forgetting themselves. (reference identified, verse number not stated)
dalil.translation: How can you tell people to do what is right and forget to do it yourselves, even though you recite the Scripture? Have you no sense?

dalil.context: Allah's great anger at saying what you do not do. (reference identified, verse number not stated)
dalil.translation: You who believe, why do you say things and then do not do them?

dalil.context: Affirmation that the Prophet SAW is not mad, by his Lord's grace. (reference identified, verse number not stated)
dalil.translation: Your Lord’s grace does not make you [Prophet] a madman:

dalil.context: The Prophet's SAW exalted character. (reference identified, verse number not stated)
dalil.translation: truly you have a strong character––

dalil.context: Surah Al-Alaq ends with prostration and drawing near. (reference identified, verse number not stated)
dalil.translation: No! Do not obey him [Prophet]: bow down in worship and draw close.

dalil.context: Allah calls 'O you wrapped up' in Al-Muzzammil. (reference identified, verse number not stated)
We will send down a heavy word, hence the need for night prayer. (reference identified, verse number not stated)
dalil.translation: We shall send a momentous message down to you.

dalil.context: Recite the Quran slowly and distinctly. (reference identified, verse number not stated)
dalil.translation: or a little more; recite the Quran slowly and distinctly:

dalil.context: The Prophet's SAW warning against venerating individuals.
dalil.translation: Do not make my grave as earlier peoples made the graves of their prophets places of worship.

sirah.era: After the first revelation, the pause in revelation
sirah.summary: Revelation paused for a while, the Prophet SAW grieved and longed for it, then saw Jibril in his true form and received Al-Muddaththir.

events.label: The pause
events.title: Revelation halts for about 40 days
events.desc: The Prophet SAW absorbed Waraqah's words and repeated Al-Alaq.

events.label: Grief
events.title: Longing for revelation
events.desc: He went to high mountains and called to the sky.

events.label: The call
events.title: A voice from the sky
events.desc: He saw the same angel seated on a throne between heaven and earth.

events.label: Collapse
events.title: Home, asking to be covered
events.desc: The Prophet SAW fell trembling and returned to Khadijah.

events.label: Al-Muddaththir
events.title: The verses of five steps come down
events.desc: Allah commanded him to rise, warn, glorify his Lord and so on.
